steps.name: QC and normalize raw counts
caveats: sample_01's low library size can inflate its variance-stabilized values or destabilize gene-set scores for that sample specifically — report its position in downstream results but do not silently exclude it without flagging
Do not filter out genes needed for hallmark gene sets before scoring; keep the full gene set post low-count filtering only if it removes genes uniformly at very low expression
steps.question: Given the 12000 x 12 raw Salmon gene-count matrix for 6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control colon samples, what is a normalized, log-scale expression matrix suitable for single-sample gene-set scoring, and how does the low-library sample_01 (~4x below median library size) affect that normalization?
acceptance_criteria: Raw counts.csv (gene symbol column + 12 sample columns) and metadata.csv (12 rows, condition column) are loaded and matched by sample ID
Library sizes per sample are computed and reported, explicitly flagging sample_01's low depth relative to the median
A normalized expression matrix (e.g. DESeq2 variance-stabilizing transformation or log2-CPM) is produced with genes as rows (gene symbol) and 12 samples as columns
Output normalized matrix and a QC summary table (library sizes, any samples flagged) are saved to disk

steps.name: GSVA hallmark pathway activity scoring
caveats: Confirm the hallmark GMT file is present in the reference store before running (organism: human) and report the exact set count and gene identifier space used
GSVA on 12 samples has limited power for kcdf choice; use the Gaussian kernel appropriate for continuous log-expression/VST input, not raw counts
steps.question: What is the GSVA-based pathway activity score for each of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets in each of the 12 colon samples (6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control)?
acceptance_criteria: GSVA is run on the normalized expression matrix from T1S1 using the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols)
Output is a pathway (50 rows) x sample (12 columns) activity score matrix, saved as a CSV
Gene symbol matching rate between the expression matrix and hallmark gene sets is reported (fraction of hallmark genes found in the expression data)
sample_01's scores are inspected and any outlier behavior attributable to its low library size is noted in the output report

steps.name: Differential pathway activity test (UC-inflamed vs control) and heatmap
caveats: With n=6 per group, treat p-values as exploratory; note in the report that this is a small, single-batch cohort with no replication or multi-cohort validation
Do not overinterpret sample_01's individual pathway scores as biological signal given its documented library-size anomaly
steps.question: Which of the 50 Hallmark pathway activity scores differ significantly between UC-inflamed and control colon samples, and what does a heatmap of the full hallmark activity matrix across all 12 samples look like when annotated by condition?
acceptance_criteria: A limma moderated t-test (or equivalent) is applied to the GSVA score matrix from T1S2 comparing UC-inflamed (n=6) vs control (n=6), producing a per-pathway effect size, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value
Results table of all 50 hallmark pathways ranked by adjusted p-value is saved as CSV

A heatmap of the sample x hallmark activity score matrix is generated with samples annotated by condition (UC-inflamed vs control) and, ideally, library-size flag for sample_01; pathways ordered by differential significance or hierarchically clustered
Heatmap image file is saved (e.g. PNG/PDF) and referenced in the output

plan.title: UC vs control colon: hallmark pathway activity scoring
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq raw Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 13 samples; one column is likely a gene-symbol column making it 12 samples) for 6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control colon samples, unpaired, single batch. sample_01 has ~4x lower library size than the median and needs explicit QC handling before normalization rather than silent inclusion. The question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score (not a two-group DE gene list) and a heatmap of hallmark activity across samples showing which pathways separate the groups. This is a single-sample gene-set scoring problem, so GSVA (or ssGSEA) is the natural choice over standard DE+ORA, since it yields one continuous score per sample per gene set rather than a binary DE call. Plan: (1) normalize raw counts to a variance-stabilized/log expression matrix suitable for GSVA, flagging the low-library sample rather than silently dropping it; (2) run GSVA with the MSigDB human hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols, confirmed present in refs) on the normalized matrix to get a sample x pathway activity score matrix; (3) test each hallmark pathway's activity score for UC vs control separation (moderated t-test via limma on GSVA scores, the standard downstream test) and rank pathways; (4) render a heatmap of the hallmark activity score matrix (samples as columns annotated by condition, pathways as rows) to visualize which pathways separate treated from control, ordering/highlighting pathways by the differential test.
